# PrivaTools

> Free file tools with explicit processing choices and optional accounts.

PrivaTools offers 225 tools for PDFs, images, video, audio, documents, archives, and developer tasks. The source is MIT-licensed and can be self-hosted.

## Processing and accounts

- Everyday tools and downloads are available without signing in. Accounts manage identity and developer API keys.
- Processing depends on the tool: browser-only utilities keep the input on the device; server tools upload files for isolated temporary processing in temporary per-request storage.
- Server cleanup is designed to remove temporary input and output after the response, with a background sweep for leftover files. This is a cleanup policy, not a claim of forensic erasure or instantaneous cleanup after every failure.
- AI Studio offers on-device models and user-selected external providers. Provider mode sends the selected content to that provider and may incur its own charges. Smart Redact detects locally, then uploads the PDF and approved terms to apply redactions.
- The current Vault, saved signatures, and tool preferences are browser-local. Signing in does not sync them across devices or back them up.
- Public processing has file-size, rate, resource, and tool-specific limits. Available native codecs and AI models depend on the deployment. Self-hosting has its own infrastructure costs.
- PrivaTools does not add a promotional watermark to downloads. Watermark tools add marks only when requested.
- Public pages use Google Analytics, on by default, for page visits, sessions, engagement, where visits come from and tool runs: which tool, how it ran, how many files, whether it succeeded and, for most failed runs, a fixed failure category such as "too_large" or "server". Where a visit came from is the referring site's origin, or the PrivaTools page it was opened from, and any standard utm_ campaign tags, sent only with the first page view of each page load and filtered by rules meant to keep out phone numbers, identifiers and tokens. It receives no file contents, filenames, document text, error messages or account identity; advertising features and Google Signals are off. Browsers that identify themselves as automated or headless are not measured. Visitors can turn analytics off on the privacy page.

## Authoritative pages

- [All tools](https://privatools.me/tools): Browse the current catalogue and each tool's processing notice.
- [Trust center](https://privatools.me/trust): Understand local, server, and provider processing.
- [Privacy](https://privatools.me/privacy): File handling, account data, and telemetry.
- [Security](https://privatools.me/security): Security boundaries and reporting.
- [Developer API](https://privatools.me/api): API access and key management.
- [API operation catalog](https://api.privatools.me/api/v1/operations): Public machine-readable operations, request fields, response media types, current costs, limits, and async availability. Browser-only website tools are listed as unavailable through HTTP.
- [Versioned OpenAPI](https://api.privatools.me/api/v1/openapi.json): The public v1 contract for developer and AI/workflow integrations. Processing requires a PrivaTools API key; discovery does not.
- [About](https://privatools.me/about): Project context and source code.
- [Source code](https://github.com/ethereaglehq/privatools): Implementation and issue tracker.

- [.env Validator](https://privatools.me/tools/env-validator): Lint .env files for syntax and risky values
- [JSON to CSV Schema](https://privatools.me/tools/json-to-csv-schema): Infer JSON schema and export flattened CSV
- [Mute Video](https://privatools.me/tools/mute-video): Strip the audio track from any video
- [Reverse Video](https://privatools.me/tools/reverse-video): Play your video backwards (audio reversed too)
- [Video Speed Changer](https://privatools.me/tools/video-speed): Speed up or slow down a video, 0.25× to 4×
- [Audio Trimmer](https://privatools.me/tools/audio-trim): Cut a clip out of any audio file
- [Image Color Palette](https://privatools.me/tools/image-palette): Extract dominant colors from any image
- [Pixelate / Blur Image](https://privatools.me/tools/pixelate-image): Censor a whole image with mosaic or Gaussian blur
- [Rotate Image](https://privatools.me/tools/rotate-image): Rotate JPG, PNG, or WEBP by 90°, 180°, 270°, or any angle
- [Flip Image](https://privatools.me/tools/flip-image): Mirror an image horizontally or vertically

## Guides

- [PrivaTools Journal](https://privatools.me/blog): Practical guides, limitations, and sources.

- [remove.bg is moving to Canva: choosing your next workflow](https://privatools.me/blog/remove-bg-canva-alternative): Choose around the result you need: a standalone transparent PNG or a cutout inside a larger design workflow. Test a representative image, understand its processing path and keep the original before changing tools.
- [From a Markdown file to a clean HTML document](https://privatools.me/blog/markdown-editor-to-html-guide): Open your .md file from home or in Markdown Editor & HTML, review the live preview, and save the format you need. This editor works in the browser. Its supported Markdown subset is deliberately smaller than a full publishing system.
- [Turn Markdown into a PDF you can actually share](https://privatools.me/blog/markdown-to-pdf-layout-checklist): Keep the Markdown source, convert a copy with Markdown to PDF, then review the downloaded pages. The editor’s local HTML preview and the server-generated PDF are different outputs with different layout and privacy considerations.
- [Use PrivaTools with—or without—an account](https://privatools.me/blog/passkeys-and-optional-accounts): You can use interactive file tools without signing in. An account supports account-specific features such as API key management. Passkeys are an optional sign-in method when enabled, and signing in does not turn local drafts or Vault data into a cloud backup.
- [Where your files go when you run a tool](https://privatools.me/blog/where-your-files-go): Selecting a file is not the same as uploading it. The tool and selected mode determine the next step: browser computation, a PrivaTools server job, or a direct AI provider request. Read that disclosure before you run the task.
- [Batch or Pipeline? Choose the shape of your task](https://privatools.me/blog/batch-or-pipeline-how-to-choose): Batch applies one supported operation to multiple inputs. Pipeline chains compatible steps so one output becomes the next input. Start with one accepted sample, and inspect partial failures or intermediate choices before scaling up.
- [Build a document workflow you can trust twice](https://privatools.me/blog/repeatable-document-workflow): Keep originals, define the output, test a small sample, and record the settings that produced an accepted result. Reusing a workflow saves setup; it does not remove the need to check each new collection.
- [How PDF chat handles your document text](https://privatools.me/blog/chat-with-pdf-free-private): PrivaTools PDF chat extracts text in the browser, then sends document text and your question directly to the BYOK provider. The raw file does not pass through PrivaTools, but the content is transmitted to the selected provider.
- [On-device AI and BYOK: two different processing choices](https://privatools.me/blog/ai-pdf-tools-no-upload-byok): On-device AI computes in your browser after loading its model. BYOK calls your selected provider with your content. Both give you a choice, but only the on-device mode keeps that computation local.
- [How to remove an image background on your device](https://privatools.me/blog/remove-background-without-uploading): Background Remover supports server and on-device engines. Select “On this device” before running if you want local processing; the current default is the server engine. The local model needs an initial download.
- [How to transcribe audio with a local or provider engine](https://privatools.me/blog/transcribe-audio-free-no-upload): Local transcription uses a downloaded model on your device. BYOK transcription sends audio to a supported provider endpoint. In either case, verify names, numbers and unclear speech against the recording.
- [OCR a scanned PDF: choose the right engine and output](https://privatools.me/blog/ocr-scanned-pdf-free-three-ways): OCR recognises text in page images. Choose an engine based on the output you need and an acceptable processing path; do not assume every engine returns the same searchable PDF, layout or accuracy.
- [How to translate PDF text and choose its processing path](https://privatools.me/blog/translate-pdf-free-private): PrivaTools translation has local and BYOK modes. Local models support specific language pairs; a provider mode sends extracted text to the chosen endpoint. The result is a translation of extracted text, not a promise to preserve the original PDF layout.
- [Bring your own AI key: a careful setup guide](https://privatools.me/blog/bring-your-own-ai-key-guide): Add a supported provider key in AI Studio, verify the endpoint and model, and try non-sensitive sample input. BYOK sends content to that provider; its billing and data policy apply. Save the key in this browser only if that suits your device.
- [How to batch-process files without losing track of results](https://privatools.me/blog/batch-process-files-free): Batch repeats the same supported operation across a set of files. Test one file first, use the current queue limits, and check each result. A partly completed batch should not be treated as a complete delivery.
- [Choosing a PDF chat alternative by its data path](https://privatools.me/blog/chatpdf-alternatives-private): Ask where document text goes, which provider receives it and what is retained. A raw PDF staying local does not make provider chat an on-device operation. Test extraction and answers with a non-sensitive sample.
- [PrivaTools and ihatepdf: check what “local” means for each tool](https://privatools.me/blog/privatools-vs-ihatepdf): A raw file can stay in the browser while extracted text is sent to an AI provider. Compare each selected tool and mode: ihatepdf documents this distinction for PDF chat, and PrivaTools BYOK chat also sends document text to the chosen provider.
- [PrivaTools and Sejda: a guide to choosing a PDF editor](https://privatools.me/blog/privatools-vs-sejda): Choose by the edit you need and the properties the export must preserve. Read the current Sejda sources and PrivaTools processing disclosure, then test a representative document rather than relying on an old task quota.
- [PrivaTools and Smallpdf: choosing for everyday file work](https://privatools.me/blog/privatools-vs-smallpdf): Try the precise operation you need and inspect its download. Check current Smallpdf information and PrivaTools disclosures; neither visual polish nor a “free” label settles file privacy or output suitability.
- [PrivaTools and iLovePDF: compare the workflow, not the headline](https://privatools.me/blog/privatools-vs-ilovepdf): Compare the exact operation, output and processing path. PrivaTools uses both browser and server tools; iLovePDF documents its own file-handling model. Current product sources belong ahead of old pricing or quota claims.
- [What browser-local file processing does—and does not—mean](https://privatools.me/blog/how-local-first-works): Browser-local processing means the selected operation computes on your device. It does not describe every tool on the website. PrivaTools uses browser, server and chosen-provider processing depending on the task and mode.
- [What deletion means for a server-processed file](https://privatools.me/blog/what-deleted-means): PrivaTools server tasks use temporary files and cleanup after the response, with a janitor for leftovers. Cleanup is an implementation behaviour, not a guarantee of instantaneous erasure after every failure or deletion of copies on your own device.
- [Five questions to ask a file tool’s privacy policy](https://privatools.me/blog/reading-privacy-policies): Look for the processing destination, retention, third-party providers, account data and optional storage. Read the clauses that apply to the feature you use; a short headline cannot stand in for the full workflow.
- [How to summarise a PDF with an on-device or provider model](https://privatools.me/blog/ai-pdf-summarizer-browser-2026): PrivaTools offers an on-device summariser and a BYOK provider mode. The local mode downloads model files and computes in the browser; provider mode sends extracted text to your selected provider. Neither mode guarantees a complete or accurate summary.
- [Looking for an iLovePDF alternative? Start with the task](https://privatools.me/blog/ilovepdf-alternatives-2026): Identify what you want to change: a task restriction, an output capability, a processing path or the interface. Then compare that exact requirement with current product information and a sample file.
- [A practical checklist for checking PDF redactions](https://privatools.me/blog/redact-pdf-permanently-guide): Inspect the exported file, not just the editor preview. Check visible regions, text extraction, repeated references and other document content; a successful apply message does not certify that every sensitive detail was found.
- [How to evaluate privacy claims in online PDF tools](https://privatools.me/blog/online-pdf-tools-tracking-you): Ask specific questions about file contents and other service data. Uploading a file is not automatically tracking, and a no-upload tool can still make ordinary network requests. Read the feature’s disclosure rather than inferring motives.
- [How to convert HEIC photos to JPG, PNG or PDF](https://privatools.me/blog/heic-conversion-guide-2026): Use JPG for a widely compatible photo, PNG when you need its image characteristics, and PDF to package an image as a document. Keep the original HEIC file and inspect the converted result.
- [How to decode a JWT without mistaking it for verification](https://privatools.me/blog/decode-jwt-tokens-safely-guide): Decoding a signed JWT shows its header and payload; it does not prove who issued it. Signature, algorithm, issuer, audience and time checks belong in a trusted verifier. Avoid using real production tokens as examples.
- [How to edit a PDF without creating an account](https://privatools.me/blog/edit-pdf-online-free-no-sign-up): Use Edit PDF for visible additions, a form tool for actual fields, and Redact PDF for removing sensitive content. Adding text or a white box is not the same as changing the original text beneath it.
- [How to split a PDF into useful sections](https://privatools.me/blog/split-pdf-online-free): Use Split PDF to divide a document, or Extract Pages when you need one selection. Check physical page positions against printed page numbers, then inspect each downloaded result.
- [How to redact sensitive information from a PDF](https://privatools.me/blog/redact-pdf-free-guide): Use the redaction tool, apply the selected regions, and verify the downloaded output. A black rectangle added by a drawing or annotation tool can leave the original content underneath.
- [Choosing a free PDF editor: what to test before committing](https://privatools.me/blog/best-free-online-pdf-editors-2026): Choose by the kind of edit, not a “best editor” badge. Test a representative page and its download, especially when form fields, underlying text, accessibility or signed documents matter.
- [How to compress a PDF while keeping it readable](https://privatools.me/blog/compress-pdf-without-losing-quality): Start with a balanced preset, keep the original, and inspect small text, diagrams and scanned pages in the result. Lossy compression changes image data; there is no universal percentage saving or guarantee of identical quality.
- [How to merge PDF files in the right order](https://privatools.me/blog/merge-pdf-files-online-free): Add the PDFs, put the files in reading order, run the merge, and inspect the first and last pages of each section. Merging in PrivaTools uses its server; an account is not required for the interactive tool.
- [How to choose a free PDF toolkit in 2026](https://privatools.me/blog/best-free-pdf-tools-2026): Start with the task and the file’s sensitivity. Then check the current tool page, export restrictions, processing path and output. This is a selection guide, not a claim that we benchmarked every product.
- [How to remove a PDF password you know](https://privatools.me/blog/remove-password-from-pdf): Use Unlock PDF with the correct password and only for a document you are authorised to change. This removes protection from the new output; it does not recover an unknown password or secure the downloaded copy.
- [How to convert Word to PDF and check the layout](https://privatools.me/blog/convert-word-to-pdf-free): Convert a copy of your Word document, then inspect the generated PDF. Office conversion runs on the server and can change layout when fonts or document features differ from the source application.

## Comparisons

- [Compare file tools](https://privatools.me/compare): Choose by workflow, processing location, and trade-offs.

- [PrivaTools and remove.bg](https://privatools.me/compare/remove-bg): remove.bg's website closes on 1 December 2026 as background removal moves to Canva. Its credits, limits and API compared with PrivaTools' free remover.
- [PrivaTools and iLovePDF](https://privatools.me/compare/ilovepdf): iLovePDF's free Basic plan limits files per task and file size, and Premium adds desktop tools and mobile access; PrivaTools is free with open code.
- [PrivaTools and Smallpdf](https://privatools.me/compare/smallpdf): Smallpdf's free plan limits daily downloads and AI use, and Pro bundles Sign.com and a Windows app. PrivaTools is free with open code. Plans and data compared.
- [PrivaTools and Adobe Acrobat](https://privatools.me/compare/adobe-acrobat): Most Adobe Acrobat online tools allow one free transaction without signing in, and editing existing text needs a paid plan; PrivaTools is free with no account.
- [PrivaTools and Sejda PDF](https://privatools.me/compare/sejda): Sejda PDF limits free use to three tasks an hour and sells Web and Desktop passes; PrivaTools has no task quota. Limits, data paths and tools compared.
- [PrivaTools and PDF24](https://privatools.me/compare/pdf24): PDF24 is free and funded by advertising, with online tools on EU servers and an offline Windows app; PrivaTools is open source. Costs and data paths compared.
- [PrivaTools and Foxit PDF Editor](https://privatools.me/compare/foxit): Foxit PDF Editor costs from $129.99 a year, with a perpetual option and free online converters; PrivaTools is free and open source. Editing and AI compared.
- [PrivaTools and LightPDF](https://privatools.me/compare/lightpdf): LightPDF pairs PDF tools with AI paid for in credits, and its free plan starts with sign-up; PrivaTools' document AI uses your own key or on-device models.
- [PrivaTools and Stirling PDF](https://privatools.me/compare/stirling-pdf): Stirling PDF is an open-core PDF editor with desktop apps and paid Team plans; PrivaTools is a web toolbox whose own code is MIT-licensed. Plans compared.
- [PrivaTools and DocHub](https://privatools.me/compare/dochub): DocHub is an online editor for signing and forms, with three free uses a month of core features; PrivaTools needs no account but has no sign requests.
- [PrivaTools and PDFescape](https://privatools.me/compare/pdfescape): PDFescape's free online editor takes 10 MB, 100-page PDFs and stores them on US servers; PrivaTools is free and open source. Limits and storage compared.
- [PrivaTools and Nitro PDF](https://privatools.me/compare/nitro-pdf): Nitro PDF is a paid desktop editor for Windows and Mac with a 14-day trial and free online converters; PrivaTools is free in the browser. Editing compared.
- [PrivaTools and TinyWow](https://privatools.me/compare/tinywow): TinyWow offers free PDF, image, video and AI writing tools, with paid plans that list no ads; PrivaTools has no ads and is open source. Plans and data compared.
- [PrivaTools and ihatepdf.cv](https://privatools.me/compare/ihatepdf): ihatepdf.cv runs most PDF tools in the browser but sends text to AI services for chat and summaries; PrivaTools mixes browser and server tools.
